newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares close firmer ahead of Telecom result.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares close firmer ahead of Telecom result.

text.p: * New Zealand shares rally in afternoon trade
* Telecom leads mkt higher ahead of Thursday's profit result
* Enerco leaps 25 cents after strong half-year profit
New Zealand shares rallied to a higher close on Wednesday, inspired by Telecom's strong performance ahead of its half-year profit result.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended 17.14 points stronger at 2,342.94, with Telecom up nine cents at NZ$7.62.

"Clearly people are getting set before the result tomorrow, it's pretty critical," said Neville Todd at County Natwest. He said there was an expectation that Telecom would also make an announcement about a rumoured share buy-back.
"There's a potential here that people might be just getting overly excited, but I think the underlying result is the key thing to look at," Todd said.
Analysts forecast a result of between NZ$360-$375 million for the market leader in the six months to June 30 against $338.7 million for the same period last year.

Brokers said there had been good demand for Fletcher Forest, up four to $2.31, and in Fletcher Paper, up five at $2.61, while Enerco shot 25 cents higher to $6.60 after reporting an improved first-half profit of $12.89 million.

However, general market optimism had been tempered by a sluggish bond market and comments made on Monday by Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash which indicated an easing in monetary policy may not be a foregone conclusion.
"The market was possibly getting a bit ahead of itself, and Brash has just given a signal that he's concerned about fiscal expansion, concerned about the tax cuts," said Todd.
"Certainly the people who have been expecting that it (an easing) is just around the corner are probably going to be a bit disappointed."
